# RABIES POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS

Patients are given post-exposure prophylaxis based upon their risk including type of exposure, epidemiology of rabies in the area where contact occurred, circumstances of the exposure incident, species and the availability of animal involved. The Minnesota Department of Health has staff available 24/7 to consult health care providers on risk-status of individuals. They can be contacted by phone at 651-201-5414. Refer to link below for more information.

[Minnesota Department of Health Guide on Animal Bites and Rabies Risk](orz-gtx-abx-mdh-animal-bites-and-rabies-risk)

Discussion with Infectious Diseases inpatient attending by phone is highly recommended. Use the link below to obtain the pager number for on-call staff.

[Infectious Diseases On-Call Schedule](orz-min-on-call-schedule)

# Wound cleansing

All post-exposure prophylaxis should begin with immediate thorough cleansing of all wounds with soap and water. After cleansing, use povidine-iodine solution to irrigate the wounds.

[Povidine-iodine irrigation solution](psczid-povidine-iodine-soln-wound-cleanse-one-time-dose)

# Patients without history of rabies vaccination

After wound cleansing, administer rabies immune globulin and first dose of rabies vaccine series immediately.

[Rabies immune globulin STAT < AND > rabies vaccine STAT](orz-set-abx-op-rabies-igg-and-vaccine-series)

Administer second, third and fourth doses of rabies vaccine series on days 3, 7, and 14. An additional dose is given on day 28 for immunocompromised patients.

# Patients with history of rabies vaccination

Patients with a history of complete pre-exposure vaccination regimen and a documented antibody response to the rabies virus, do not require rabies immune globulin administration. If the patient does not meet these criteria, treat as a patient without history of rabies vaccination above. If patient does meet these criteria, after wound cleansing, administer first dose of rabies vaccine series.

[Rabies vaccine STAT](orz-set-abx-op-rabies-stat-and-vaccine-series)

Administer second dose of rabies vaccine series on day 3.

# Tetanus Prophylaxis

In bite wounds that break the skin, tetanus vaccine is indicated if patient has received <3 doses of tetanus vaccine or immunization history is unknown. Tetanus immune globulin is also indicated in these patients if they have a tetanus prone wound. For patients with 3 or more documented tetanus vaccine doses, tetanus vaccine is indicated if >5 years since last booster in tetanus prone wounds and indicated if >10 years since last booster in non-tetanus-prone wounds.

[Tetanus and Diphtheria \(Td\) vaccine booster dose STAT](psczid-tetanus-diptheria-vaccine-one-dose-stat)
